Predictions and inference for two-component models

Source: R/count-methods.R
predict.fastglm_hurdle.Rd

The response prediction averages over both components. For hurdle models, `count` is the conditional mean among positive counts and `zero` is the probability of observing zero. For zero-inflated models, `count` is the mean of the untruncated count distribution. Prediction standard errors use the delta method and include uncertainty in theta when it is estimated.

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_hurdle'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob", "link"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  at = 0:10,
  sink = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fastglm_zi'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "count", "zero", "prob", "link"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  at = 0:10,
  sink = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a hurdle, zero-inflated, or two-part fit.

newdata

optional data frame or list of design matrices named `count` and `zero`, optionally with `offset=list(count=...,zero=...)`. With a streaming model, omitting it rereads the fitted source.

type

prediction scale: marginal response, count-component mean, zero probability, probability masses, or component linear predictors.

se.fit

return delta-method standard errors.

at

nonnegative integer counts for `type = "prob"`.

sink

optional function of `(value, chunk_index)` for a streaming fit. It receives each block of predictions so that results can be written or summarized without retaining predictions for all observations in memory.

...

additional arguments.

Value

Predicted values, or a `fastglm_prediction` list with `fit` and `se.fit`; see fastglm-prediction-methods for printing and table extraction.
